subject: surgery
title: Renal Cell Carcinoma and Benign Renal Tumours

steps.tx: The commonest malignant kidney tumour in adults is **renal cell carcinoma**. It arises from the lining cells of the kidney tubules and grows silently for years. Many cases are now found by chance on scans done for other reasons. It is about twice as common in men, and smoking, obesity and long term dialysis all raise the risk.
steps.say: Renal cell carcinoma is the commonest adult kidney cancer and many cases now appear by chance on scans.

vis.alt: Renal cell carcinoma specimen showing clear cell tumour.
vis.caption: Renal cell carcinoma: clear cell tumour of the kidney. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The commonest microscopic type, with cells full of clear looking glycogen and fat, is **clear cell carcinoma**. It links strongly to loss of the von Hippel-Lindau gene on chromosome 3. This loss drives blood vessel growth within the tumour. Loss of chromosome 3p is the hallmark genetic change, found in most clear cell tumours even when they are small.
steps.say: Clear cell carcinoma follows von Hippel-Lindau gene loss, which drives rich blood vessel growth in the tumour.

steps.tx: Loose blood in urine, loin pain and a palpable mass together form the **classic triad**. All three appear together in only a minority of patients, usually with advanced disease. Any painless visible blood in urine still needs full investigation. The triad is a late sign, and most modern cases are found incidentally before any of the three appears.
steps.say: The classic triad of blood in urine, loin pain and a mass appears together in only a minority of patients.

steps.tx: A left sided varicocele that does not empty on lying down suggests **left varicocele** from tumour blocking the left renal vein. Tumour can grow as a cord inside the vein toward the heart. This venous growth changes staging and surgical planning. The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein, which is why a new left varicocele in an older man demands a kidney scan.
steps.say: A left varicocele that stays full on lying down warns of tumour blocking the left renal vein.

steps.tx: Extra red blood cell production driven by tumour erythropoietin is **paraneoplastic polycythaemia**. Renal cancers also cause fever, weight loss and high calcium without any spread. These general effects are called paraneoplastic syndromes. High calcium comes from a parathyroid hormone related protein made by the tumour, and it settles after nephrectomy when no bone spread exists.
steps.say: Paraneoplastic polycythaemia comes from tumour made erythropoietin, one of several general effects of kidney cancer.

steps.tx: Reversible liver test disturbance without liver spread is called **Stauffer syndrome**. Blood tests improve after the kidney tumour is removed. Its presence does not by itself mean cancer has spread to the liver. It is an exam trap: abnormal liver tests with a normal liver scan should not delay removal of the kidney tumour.
steps.say: Stauffer syndrome disturbs liver tests without liver spread, and tests improve after the tumour is removed.

steps.tx: An inherited condition with kidney cancers and cysts in many organs is **von Hippel-Lindau** disease. Affected people develop tumours in the kidney, adrenal gland, pancreas and back of the eye. Family screening finds lesions early. Eye lesions are retinal haemangioblastomas, so regular eye checks sit alongside kidney scans in family surveillance programmes.
steps.say: Von Hippel-Lindau disease causes kidney cancers with tumours in the adrenal, pancreas and eye, so families need screening.

vis.alt: Tuberous sclerosis complex features including renal angiomyolipomas.
vis.caption: Inherited tumour syndromes affecting the kidney. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Complete removal of the kidney with its surrounding fat is a **radical nephrectomy**. It remains standard for large tumours confined to the kidney. The adrenal gland is removed only when involved or at high risk. The operation also removes the fatty envelope around the kidney, and tumour growing inside the vein may require opening the vein itself.
steps.say: Radical nephrectomy removes the kidney with surrounding fat and stays standard for large confined tumours.

vis.alt: Partial nephrectomy for renal carcinoma preserving kidney tissue.
vis.caption: Nephron sparing surgery for suitable kidney tumours. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Removal of only the tumour with a margin of normal tissue is a **partial nephrectomy**. It preserves kidney function and suits small tumours, single kidneys and bilateral disease. Warm ischaemia time is kept short to protect the remaining kidney. Keeping warm ischaemia, the clamped blood flow time, under about 25 minutes limits permanent loss of kidney function.
steps.say: Partial nephrectomy removes only the tumour to preserve kidney function in small or bilateral disease.

steps.tx: A targeted drug blocking blood vessel growth signals used in advanced disease is **sunitinib**. Modern treatment often pairs such drugs with immune therapy. Benign fat and muscle tumours called angiomyolipomas, linked to tuberous sclerosis, usually need treatment only when large or bleeding, while simple round oncocytomas may only need surveillance.
steps.say: Sunitinib blocks vessel growth in advanced cancer, while benign angiomyolipomas usually need treatment only when large.
